cancellationSafetyRequirements: Passed-by is not obsolete. Reversal, density changes, panel/reflow changes and future smaller-thumbnail layouts can expose it again. The earlier count of passed-by requests does not establish the number outside a protected range.

Protect visible/eager/mounted demand, shared-source consumers and pending navigation/restoration targets. A candidate protected nearby range must be justified in result space against supported layout exposure, not guessed from pixels or current density alone.

Recheck source/request generation and current demand immediately before abort; retire stale decisions after direction, scope, density, width or navigation changes. Cancellation must not kill a coalesced current consumer.

Cancel only still-pending work; preserve completed cache entries and metadata/publication. Prove immediate re-admission on re-exposure and avoid permanent failed-image state or duplicate/restart storms.

First establish local cancellation and reacquisition behavior, including shared ownership, rapid reversal, density/panel changes and completion races. A failed request event alone does not prove backend savings or a live scrolling improvement.

Live cancellation requires separate operator approval; hold B2/eager/geometry/resource policies fixed and compare useful progress/current readiness, frames, stability, metadata delay and cost together.

For Justified, bounded earlier availability is promising for keeping re-layout unseen, but1000ms plus a ready page is a conditional result, not a selected product policy. Cost the initial page and navigation latency explicitly; retain adverse frame/readiness observations.
True-ratio fragments are a separately investigated late-arrival alternative, not a general lifecycle or blocking fix. No incoming square slots or rejected freeze may be adopted.

Any selected implementation must combine applied-input anchor checks, all-visible-box stability, correct ratios, frame/media costs and full lifecycle/navigation proof; current independent controls do not establish that combined guarantee.

b2GeometryLifetime20261021.head: 0ccff3c6be0381fa993cc76f9915d90c004488c6
b2GeometryLifetime20261021.question: Can a visibility-scoped block hold keep truthful dimensions, release without moving other visible blocks, and avoid surviving incompatible navigation?

conditions.data: Existing seamCorpus, mixed ratios including 10:1 and 0.67:1; synthetic IDs only. No live reads or browser use.
conditions.backward: Four cases: 390/1120px, indexed/seek. Seed global48..191, partial44..191, completed0..191. Exactly4 of48 boundary dimensions initially known. Test-only spy holds original packing inputs for one build; actual dimensions remain authoritative.
conditions.forward: Two cases at390/1120px: partial0..51 then completed0..143; test-only hold of the second block. First known row is a negative control, not presumed unstable.
conditions.lifecycle: One case characterizes existing factual dimension snapshot through resize, re-entry, full-block eviction, return with missing boundary dimensions, different query, disjoint seek, regime change and reorder.
conditions.scope: Only the existing unit test file changed under src. No runtime hold state, product policy, metadata-fetch change, browser fixture or campaign-history change. Mocked packing is always restored.

findings: Holding the original block inputs retains the four original known-image box shapes while real new dimensions publish separately. Newly known images can occupy square provisional boxes despite nonsquare authoritative ratios.
Original-cohort departure is insufficient: a row of newly known images in the same held block can be visible after all four original images leave; release changes those new boxes.

After releasing the prefix block, all items48..191 retain left/width/height and receive one identical vertical translation in all four mixed-ratio controls. This is geometry evidence for existing compensation, not DOM timing or unclamped-scroll certification.
The first known forward row remains identical after real dimensions replace estimates at both widths. Partial-block status alone is not evidence that a visible row needs a hold.

Existing factual snapshots preserve real ratios through width changes and compatible re-entry, drop fully evicted blocks, and discard incompatible query/overlap/regime/reorder context. They contain no presentation lifetime or navigation generations.
b2GeometryLifetime20261021.refutedExpectation: The first forward known row was initially asserted to move. Both widths disproved that assertion (41 passed,2 failed in the initial43-case file run). The retained tests assert its stability, not a relaxed tolerance; acquisition recommendation now requires an actual retained-visible-box change.
b2GeometryLifetime20261021.decision: Recommend a conditional mounted-view presentation hold with truthful dimensions kept separate, whole-block guarded offscreen release, explicit epoch invalidation and current-window state bounds. This is not product selection; temporary containment/letterboxing requires acceptance and actual-renderer lifecycle proof.

subsequentOperatorDecision.reason: Operator explicitly rejected newly arriving images inheriting provisional square slots. The preceding decision is historical research context, not current authority. No replacement solution selected.
subsequentOperatorDecision.scopeClarification: Positive calibrated Justified movement was observed under current product policy during backward prepend, not only under proposed B2. Forward packing shares the dependency but equivalent visible movement is not established by the first-row negative controls.

alternatives: Pre-exposure dimension completion not selected: it needs a waiting/exposure/read contract to guarantee complete boundary data; prediction alone cannot guarantee it. No new latency measurements.
Original-cohort-only release refuted; independent row/fragment splicing remains an unselected, more complex alternative if provisional-slot legibility is unacceptable.
Permanent/cross-density box retention, timer/media/idle expiry, guessed ratios and global key changes not selected.

validation.notRun: No browser suites, build, campaign/dry run, live-media observation or independent product review. Prior27 app/347 harness/54 browser fixture results remain historical checkpoint evidence, not reruns.

proofGaps: No lifetime implementation exists: scroll-triggered release, aborted renders and generation ownership remain unverified.
No approval or actual-media proof of provisional-slot legibility; object-contain prevents distortion/cropping but can significantly reduce displayed image area.

Partial eviction, simultaneous held blocks, true-end/start topology, clamp behavior, density/width/seek/history transitions and release-triggered workload need actual-owner tests if implementation is selected.
No universal no-flash, single-frame, native-input or performance guarantee follows from pure geometry or earlier sparse filmstrips.

b2StabilityFilmstrip20261021.head: 0ccff3c6be0381fa993cc76f9915d90c004488c6
b2StabilityFilmstrip20261021.question: Do already-visible thumbnails show intermediate content or move when a backward page publishes, and which mechanism explains a positive finding?

conditions.application: Current product policy and source files unchanged; local app on3041,70000 synthetic records,1000-image retention. No live-service reads. B1/F1, two lower eager rows, five-row overscan and upper/rest lazy behavior fixed.
conditions.images: Locally generated400x300 PNGs with complementary color patches and black position markers.512-color encoding distinguishes this bounded prepend neighborhood, not arbitrary image identities across the whole corpus. No real thumbnail URLs, credentials or screenshots saved.
conditions.capture: CDP screencast starts before publication; PNGs stay in memory, bounded by128 frames/16MiB. Frame timestamps converted to milliseconds after store publication. At most128 target points. Browser-native PNG decoding and pixel classification performed after capture.
conditions.calibration: Synthetic classifier detects wrong content, blank content and8px displacement. Each app capture separately injects a wrong image and8px displacement for150ms, restores both, and requires their detection. Important CSS priority makes the displacement effective; original value/priority restored. Deliberate errors excluded from normal cohort observations.
conditions.positions: Edge controls stop at the temporary loaded-data wall; interior controls place the viewport around buffer-local index96 and admit a legitimate programmatic backward read. No blanket unmarked-demand veto. Both layouts retain their normal compensation.
conditions.transport: Normal routes use local generated images. Inline uses data URLs to remove image HTTP transport, not to emulate production cache policy. Held-repeat arms would delay repeat requests for target images by200ms, but no such requests occurred: treatment unsupported, not proof of delay tolerance.
conditions.counterfactual: Justified-only frozen-boundary arm substitutes the48 original ratios in one affected block in the intercepted fixture module response. It holds estimates during this observation only; no product toggle, key change, permanent freeze or geometry-lifetime design selected.
conditions.limits: Compositor delivery is sparse, not every physical display frame. Calibration demonstrates150ms wrong-image/shift detection, not guaranteed single-frame detection. Large capture gaps include unchanged-screen intervals and cannot certify absence of shorter glitches. Unknown pixels mean an unclassifiable complementary pair, not necessarily blank imagery. Headless/local data and marked PNGs do not certify live photo performance or native trackpad behavior.
conditions.rounding: All saved numeric fields rounded to three decimals. Frame times are action-relative, not epoch timestamps. Cases are individual controls, not population-tail estimates.

findings: Both layouts' fully known interior controls retained the sampled image colors and anchor marker through publication, despite DOM image replacement. This is bounded evidence, not a universal no-flash guarantee.

Justified's visible boundary image changed box geometry while the central anchor remained stable. Same ordinal-100/block-144:4 known dimensions became48, and44 default square ratios became4:3. Its box moved horizontally and shrank; a sampled point moved95.805px horizontally/14.38px vertically. Its own source stayed correct; another image occupied the old screen point. This is an observed boundary-layout change, not a proven wrong-source flash.

Holding only that block's original ratios removed the sampled movement and changed/unknown identity pairs while DOM replacement still occurred. That isolates a specific geometry cause, not a reason for a global key rewrite or generic packing diagnosis. The control deliberately retains provisional shapes for new neighbors and is not shippable as-is.

No already-visible target image was re-requested. In ordinary interior controls,30 Grid/55 Justified image requests were all for new-page records outside both the original buffer and final mounted rows. Intermediate render-state admission is a lead; extra speculative image work is not automatically harmful or wasted and is not a production byte estimate.

The repeat-request delay arms did not exercise their delay. Their stable pictures cannot establish tolerance of slow repeated image fetches. Inline transport-free controls are separately labelled, not presented as a verified production warm-cache model.

Centre-anchor correctness alone is insufficient for the operator's broader no-swimming goal. The boundary image can move and resize even with a stable anchor. Before product selection, define how visible provisional geometry survives new dimensions and when it may be recomputed.
exclusions: Initial app displacement calibration applied0px because ordinary inline translate did not override animation. Those captures were rejected; the repaired control verifies an actual8px displacement and restores CSS value/priority.

Classifier revision1 used a single color patch, which could misidentify blended colors. Final records require a complementary pair; earlier single-patch colors are not evidence of a wrong image source.

An early transport-control attempt included deliberately injected loading in its normal baseline. Calibration intervals are now excluded from cohort assertions while retained in the compositor positive controls.
Earlier identical-photo fixtures cannot distinguish a wrong-thumbnail flash. Late screenshots cannot reconstruct earlier paint. Neither limitation is repaired retroactively in historical records.

validation.appFixtures: 27 non-comparison local app fixtures passed; B2 policy comparison studies not replayed
validation.classifier: Failing-first synthetic control then passed for wrong image, blank image and8px displacement; app captures independently detected both live calibration errors
validation.evidenceChecks: All9 final compositor cases, frame records and geometry witnesses exactly matched the completed app-run log after numeric rounding; editor diagnostics empty and whitespace checks passed
validation.scope: No product source edits, shared-app drive, live-service reads, staging/commit/push or canonical campaign-history changes

b2Publication20261021.head: 0ccff3c6be0381fa993cc76f9915d90c004488c6
b2Publication20261021.question: Does backward publication disturb images that were already visible, including at capacity during movement and reversal?

conditions.policy: Current backward admission only; one held backward page. B1/F1, two lower eager rows, upper/rest lazy, five-row overscan and retention limits unchanged. No product edits or packing changes.
conditions.data: 70000 synthetic records, uniform4:3 metadata; ordinary initial buffer300, capacity1000. Local app on3041; all service traffic blocked.
conditions.media: Existing synthetic400x300 SVG and existing image-loader/test/resources/guardian-turner.jpg, intercepted locally at unique per-image fixture URLs. Original visible cohort explicitly loaded/decoded before capture. Routing disables ordinary HTTP caching; this is not a production warm-cache or CDN cost model.
conditions.observation: Browser-local identity cohort, at most128 images and512 frame samples; URLs/identities never serialized.300ms no-publication baseline, then at least500ms after publication. Existing thumbnail and bounded CDP request probes; aggregate requests cover the whole window, not only retained cohort images.
conditions.moving: 400ms at-1000px/s with held page released after80ms, then400ms at+1000px/s. Publication must occur inside first driver interval. Optional applied-step trace capped at2048 excludes compensation; positions are adjusted for applied input and CSS translate.
conditions.pixels: Separate stopped JPEG controls capture a crop before publication, a hidden-image calibration and a post-publication crop. PNGs retained only in memory and compared using browser-native canvas decoding. Original native decode promise is returned unchanged; lifetime timing only. Screenshot intervention changes timing/traffic, so never pool with ordinary controls.
conditions.scope: Headless local Playwright,1720x960. No native-trackpad, real-photo population, compositor-gap duration or live performance certification. Numeric fields rounded to three decimals; exposure is a ratio. Individual runs, not population tails.

findings: Every retained cohort image acquired a replacement DOM image in both layouts, below capacity as well as at capacity. Stored URLs stayed unchanged; stationary baselines had zero readiness waits. This shared effect cannot require Justified packing and cannot be attributed solely to eviction.

Existing image/source/element-generation counters were zero in stopped runs despite wholesale replacement: they compare prior generations on the same DOM element, not identity continuity across new elements. Zero is not proof of retained nodes.

At aligned capacity, sampled anchor displacement after subtracting driven input was below1px in both layouts during continued motion/reversal; one read, bounded retention, far-end eviction and endpoint placement assertions passed. This is bounded current-policy ownership evidence, not arbitrary-speed or candidate certification.

The below-capacity Grid fixture started at column remainder1 and prepended199 images into six columns. Its303px non-anchor row change is an alignment transition, not Justified packing. Justified's19.094px non-anchor shift is retained separately; no packing diagnosis or packing change selected.

Non-pixel controls recorded zero missing/unloaded retained images at sampled frames, but gaps between samples do not prove continuous paint readiness. Publication observations reported117-150ms waits and30-70 whole-window media starts, with zero baseline starts and zero pending at end. Routed local-cache conditions prevent production refetch/byte conclusions or attribution of every request to retained images.

Pixel controls were late for the native-decode interval: both pending flags were false before capture. Hidden-image calibration was sensitive, but nearly identical post-publication pixels do not disprove an earlier blank frame. Native decode itself took1.9/2.4ms and was initiated167/147ms after publication in these instrumented controls; do not label the longer observation as native decode duration.

Screenshot/calibration controls changed request counts and sampled loading compared with ordinary controls; their exposure/frame values are not pooled. No source-key, packing, eager-band, buffer-size, prediction-budget or measurement-definition change is selected.
b2Publication20261021.nextQuestion: Is the shared publication-to-current-image-request interval a real visible disruption under validated cache conditions, and which renderer/browser step owns it? Use a bounded action-owned trace/cohort association, not a packing rewrite or a global content-key substitution. Preserve the existing seek/history protections around positional keys.

validation.appFixtures: 18 non-comparison app fixtures passed; completed B2 policy comparisons deliberately not rerun
validation.stepTrace: Failing-first control now records100px applied input while excluding80px external compensation; nine focused scroll controls passed
validation.evidenceChecks: All12 final publication rows and both pixel rows verified against the completed app-fixture log; editor diagnostics empty and diff whitespace checks passed
validation.bounds: No cohort or request overflow; sampled anchor never absent; full-capacity moving publication lies inside the driven interval; screenshots/IDs/URLs not written

Control stayed201/41924/83. This directly explains the paired-start mismatch; it does not prove a packing defect or that programmatic demand is illegitimate.

Reset velocity symmetrically immediately before measurement. No product toggle or source edit; no packing reset, changed tolerance or programmatic-demand veto.
justifiedAfterSetupRepair.matching: Same exact full-window and geometry checks as Grid; Justified starts with201 records/headroom83, capacity case1000/headroom82. Both treatment orders passed. Grid was not repeated; do not pool the two setup revisions as one run.

localValidation.savedEvidence: All20 Grid numeric records and all20 Justified numeric records individually checked against their respective completed test logs before overwrite; setup revisions retained separately

Early paired smoke checks lacked the thumbnail-enabled flag or reused tab state; no accepted pairs.

frameOnly.description: Separate fifth matched 200-image set; Justified 1200 px/s over 2800 px; fresh documents and browser cache bypass; no thumbnail/entry observers or CDP request collector; only rAF timing and a final loaded-image count

frameAttribution.description: Additional matched 200-image set; Justified 1200 px/s over 2800 px; two repetitions per arm in reversed order; no thumbnail/entry observers. Warm arms retain 200 predecoded Image objects. Hidden-warm additionally hides only img painting while preserving layout. These are diagnostic controls, not proposed UX or prefetch policies.
frameAttribution.interpretation: The extra frame cost disappears with predecoded visible media and zero new motion requests. Hiding warm media offers no consistent additional benefit; retain the 15.8ms hidden-warm outlier. This narrows the issue to runtime arrival/decode/first-display work rather than steady drawing or band calculation alone, without isolating an exact browser subsystem. Zero motion transfers do not include the cost of warming all 200 images.

conditions.browser: Playwright Chromium 151; reduced user-agent version 151.0.0.0; full browser version not captured
conditions.network: unthrottled real thumbnail delivery; browser cache bypass; upstream caches uncontrolled
conditions.data: two disjoint read-only API seeks with the existing cutoff; first 200 records per window replayed through MockDataSource; service routes blocked during replay
conditions.measurement: existing thumbnail observer; motion-only rAF intervals; fresh document per arm; initial visible images decoded before motion; runtime row/decoding attributes verified

requestAccountingLimitation.reason: The collector spanned fresh-document transitions. Carry-in grew across arms without validated document-boundary termination accounting; these values cannot establish current-document backlog, concurrency, byte cost or contention. Request cohorts are excluded from treatment conclusions.

interpretation: No reproduced lookahead frame deficit in this browser/viewport/corpus: per-run p95 was 14.8-16.7ms across all arms. Async decoding therefore has no demonstrated corrective benefit; it is not recommended from this evidence.

Both +2-row arms shifted median decode readiness ahead of entry and ended with no pending visible thumbnails in all four runs. Small blank-area differences can include initial observer settling; do not rank them as reliable policy superiority.

Current arm blank area varied from 5.556% first to 0.413% last in window 1 despite browser cache bypass. Preserve this delivery/order variation; two windows and four runs per arm are not population-tail evidence.

The prior embedded-Chromium150 1163x887 adverse frame result remains valid evidence in its own conditions. This Chromium151 1720x960 comparison changes browser, viewport and media; it does not isolate which factor explains the difference.

No further frame-only confirmation is needed to claim a fix because no fix is claimed. Ordinary +2 rows remain a candidate requiring sustained-scroll, refresh-overlap and reversal guardrails before adoption. This replay does not test API contention or certify permanent policy.

Before any later fresh-document request comparison, recreate the collector per document or explicitly validate document-boundary completion/cancellation accounting. Do not reinterpret these excluded counters as evidence of a product queue leak.

refreshLookaheadAttempt.protocol: Existing D11 helper/validator, Justified, current versus +2 downward rows/default decoding, one document and one bounded collector; policy order AB/BA/AB/BA, drained-first on odd blocks and active-first on even blocks. Existing 80ms/4Mibit/s constraints unchanged. No retries or canonical history writes.
refreshLookaheadAttempt.stopReason: Paired source query/corpus changed during block 4's +2 pair; exact mismatch was not captured before teardown. No assumption that this was specifically corpus-total drift, and no performance-regression conclusion.
refreshLookaheadAttempt.setupConfound: Block 1 current-policy drained arm began at scrollTop2897 with32 visible images; active arm and subsequent completed arms began at2690 with38. Action metrics pass existing validation, but this does not establish matched starting geometry/media demand. No treatment verdict from this incomplete, incompletely balanced set.
refreshLookaheadAttempt.nextDecision: Superseded by the approved setup correction and completed refreshLookaheadMatched experiment below. Preserve these incomplete rows separately; do not pool them with the corrected protocol.

refreshLookaheadMatched.protocol: One elected source and one document/collector throughout; four blocks with policy order current/+2, +2/current, current/+2, +2/current. Drained-first in odd blocks, active-first in even blocks. Existing D11 action observer, overlap validator, constraints and deadlines unchanged; no retries or canonical history writes.

setupCorrection.diagnosis: Alignment alone failed: source parameters, total and full ordered data window matched, but visible identities, geometry and headroom differed. Justified retains its packing origin and boundary dimensions across overlapping windows and density unmounts.
setupCorrection.method: Before each priming arm, unmount Justified, clear only its retained packing snapshot via a temporary served-module hook, and remount the unchanged prepared window. Assert records reference, offset, total and parameters unchanged. Align the elected anchor row100px below the viewport top, require stable geometry, decode initial visible media unthrottled, and reverify the browser-local identity/geometry/window/headroom signature before applying the existing constrained priming protocol.
setupCorrection.limits: This is setup normalization, not a proposed product packing change. The canonical D11 helper and workload were not modified. Historical unnormalized D11 values are not a numerical baseline for this revised setup. The original source-query/corpus guard failure did not recur and its exact cause remains unknown. One later source-election timeout also remains unexplained; a bounded setup-only diagnostic and the final comparison passed without extending deadlines.

interpretation: All block differences are candidate-minus-current within the same block. Overlap deltas are first computed active-minus-drained within each policy pair; these are not differences of campaign medians.

Median paired overlap penalties (data/placement/media) were113.95/110.6/136.3ms currently and-23.4/-21.55/-0.4ms with+2. Negative values do not prove that media load speeds up refreshes; backend/cache/order variation remains.

Absolute active-media readiness was faster with+2 in three blocks and157.7ms slower in one. Drained-media readiness was slower by109.1/0.4/57.9/66ms. Preserve the adverse sample and drained-refresh signal rather than declaring a universal win.

Drained publication also changed by168.8/-3.1/91.8/47.2ms. Candidate-minus-current post-publication media intervals were-59.7/+3.5/-33.9/+18.8ms, not a repeated delivery regression after publication. This narrows interpretation but does not assign the upstream timing variation or dismiss observed user-facing delays.

Image request starts per refresh rose73to88. At visible-media completion roughly27requests remained pending currently versus41to43with+2. Completed-byte evidence excludes those pending transfers; no total byte-cost, obsolete-demand or backend-work claim is made.

Advance ordinary+2 only to remaining sustained-scroll and Grid/reversal evaluation, retaining drained-refresh latency as an explicit unresolved guardrail. No product adoption, async hint, universal safety or different-query/seek certification follows.

scrollLookaheadMatched.protocol: Existing D10 three8s segments at1200px/s and D9 three seconds backward then1.5s forward at4000px/s, unthrottled with browser-cache bypass during measurement; upstream caches uncontrolled. Two independently elected matched-source blocks per layout/workload, policy order current/+2 then+2/current. One document/collector per case. Justified packing reset while unmounted; anchor row aligned100px below viewport top; initial visible media decoded; full starting identities/window/geometry/headroom matched within each block. No sizing, decoding, upper-band or B2 change.

incompleteAttempt.reason: Initial geometric-below-viewport policy check stopped at second block setup with Runtime policy mismatch; source parameters/total still matched. Exact failed subpredicate was not recorded. Revised verification reads the actual virtualizer range/items/row loading attributes and waits for bounded render settlement. The final run verified all treatments; it did not reproduce a geometric/logical count difference, so do not assert a specific padding cause.

interpretation: Grid endurance blank area fell from1.443-2.072% to0-0.070%. Justified early exposure fell from0.297-0.425% to0.024-0.035%, and middle from0.884-1.325% to0-0.701%; late remained2.205-2.431% with+2 versus1.942-2.103% currently. No claim of a sustained Justified loading cure.

Endurance phases achieved9560-9610px with no buffer blocking. Justified frame p95 remained16-16.8ms. Grid frame timing had an order/time shift41.7to33.4ms even in the later current arm; do not assign that whole shift to lookahead.

Late Justified media peaks were36-64 requests across both policies; one candidate ended with8pending and228.6ms longest visible wait. Boundary reuse counters and delivery durations differ between phases; no event-level causal attribution or unbounded-backlog claim follows.

Grid reversal p95 rose47.9to50.8ms and47.5to49.9ms, with319.5px and166.5px more achieved travel. First candidate also admitted2backward reads versus1; no post-stop starts or leftover refills occurred. Retain the2.4-2.9ms frame-tail trade-off instead of silently accepting it or claiming equal work.

Justified reversal blank exposure and blocking were mixed. The first current arm had650.7ms mean completed-media duration and1655.6ms maximum completed-data duration, far slower delivery than its paired candidate. Do not attribute its58.5to7.8% blank-area reduction solely to lookahead. Second pair had10.7% candidate versus8.6% current exposure and more blocking with the candidate.

All stopped viewports decoded. Their final identities/populations differed with achieved movement (including18versus24Grid images in one pair), so shorter candidate recovery times are not a same-image download-speed comparison.

Two observations per policy/case are screening evidence, not population tails, native-wheel certification or permanent-policy acceptance. Keep the earlier drained-refresh timing signal explicit. Prefer a brief manual trackpad A/B and operator trade-off decision before implementation, rather than another broad synthetic sweep or a wider band/scheduler by default.

interpretationNotes: pendingAtEntry means not loaded (complete/naturalWidth), not explicit decode or exact paint; blank exposure and decodeLead use the existing decoded-thumbnail observer.
blankPct is viewport slot area; very small treatment values can be dominated by the initial observer/decode settling frame. Do not rank tiny differences as reliable policy improvements.
Request lead is milliseconds from CDP request start to first observed slot entry; positive means the request started before entry. decodeLeadPx is measured at decode readiness, not at entry.

Requests and CDP encodedDataLength bytes include setup and recovery. kB means decimal kilobytes at the browser boundary, not backend work. Unexposed means not exposed during measured motion, not never viewed or permanently wasted.
Policy order is balanced, but upstream caches and live delivery are not frozen. Four windows are not a population tail estimate or an exhaustive aspect-ratio corpus.
Resident replay isolates image readiness and excludes real refill/eviction costs. Programmatic smooth scrolling is not native trackpad, reversal, mobile or hosted-CDN certification.

Two extra rows removed pending-at-entry images in this matrix, but faster Justified frame costs persisted without heavy observers. The additional warm controls narrow that cost to runtime media arrival; they do not certify a production loading policy.
